title: 2012 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement: Externally tangent circles with centers at points \(A\) and \(B\) have radii of lengths \(5\) and \(3,\) respectively. A line externally tangent to both circles intersects ray \(AB\) at point \(C.\) What is \(BC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be \(BC.\) Note that \(\triangle CEB\) and \(\triangle CDA\) are similar due to angle-angle (tangent lines are perpendicular to radii).

Then \[ \dfrac{x}{3} = \dfrac{8 + x}{5}. \] Cross-multiplying gives us \[ 5x = 24 + 3x \]\[ x = 12. \]

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Draw radii to the two tangent points
The two right triangles with vertex \(C\) are similar
